headline: GOLD POSTS WORST OCTOBER SINCE 2008, DOWN 7.4% — Monthly Close at $3,897; Silver Settles Below $50 for First Time Since November 2025
snippet: Gold closed October at approximately US$3,897/oz — its worst monthly close in over a year and confirming the worst October performance for the metal since the 2008 financial crisis, down approximately 7.4% for the month. Silver settled below US$50/oz for the first time since November 2025, declining over 12% in October. Three simultaneous headwinds drove the rout: strong US Q3 GDP (3.4%), rising PCE inflation (3.6% annually), and escalating Middle East tensions pushing oil prices higher — all reinforcing market pricing of a December Federal Reserve rate hike at approximately 70% probability on Polymarket. The monthly close erases gains built over the prior three months and sets up a pivotal first week of November with key central bank commentary and several major gold miner earnings releases ahead. The GLD ETF finished at a 52-week low.

headline: GRUPO MEXICO TO POUR $4-6 BILLION INTO ASARCO US COPPER EXPANSION — Three-Year Arizona Commitment Largest Domestic Copper Capex in Memory
snippet: Grupo Mexico announced plans to invest between US$4 billion and US$6 billion over the next three years to expand copper production at Asarco, its US subsidiary and operator of the Mission, Ray, and Silver Bell mines in Arizona along with the Hayden smelter. The commitment is one of the largest single copper investment packages in US history and comes as the US government continues to press for domestic critical mineral supply chain build-out ahead of potential copper tariff decisions. Production capacity growth at established open-pit operations is targeted. The announcement was made even as spot LME copper retreated to approximately US$14,140/t on Friday amid tech-driven risk-off sentiment — an irony that underscores how long-cycle mine investment decisions are made independently of short-term price noise.

headline: RIO TINTO RESUMES OYU TOLGOI UNDERGROUND AFTER 24-HOUR SEISMIC HALT — Safety Review Complete; Timeline for Full Output Not Given
snippet: Rio Tinto began restarting underground operations at its Oyu Tolgoi copper-gold mine in Mongolia on October 30 after completing a safety review following the October 29 seismic event that injured three workers and triggered a full underground halt. The company confirmed no fatalities and said operations were resuming carefully, with no timeline provided for returning to full output. The mine accounts for approximately 56% of Rio's quarterly copper output. The restart news provided some floor for copper prices heading into the weekend, although Oyu Tolgoi remains impacted by Chinese border restrictions at the Gashuunsukhait crossing that have already reduced concentrate exports by approximately 70% over the prior two weeks — a compounding logistics headwind even as underground production resumes.

headline: WORLD BANK LIFTS 2027 COPPER PRICE FORECAST BY 18% — Projects $13,000/TONNE as Structural Supply Constraints Outweigh AI Demand Doubts
snippet: The World Bank raised its 2027 average copper price forecast by approximately 18% to about US$13,000 per tonne (approximately US$5.90/lb) in its October 2026 commodity outlook, citing persistent supply-side constraints — including declining ore grades at major Chilean and Peruvian operations and years of underinvestment in new mine capacity — as more structurally significant than the current debate over AI data centre demand. The upgrade arrives in stark contrast to near-term sentiment, with spot copper trading around US$14,140/t on Friday but posting its first monthly loss since June on AI spending doubts. Chile's Cochilco independently raised its own 2026 copper price forecast to US$5.95/lb, while projecting Chilean output will fall 2.6% to 5.27 million tonnes this year due to first-half operational weakness at major mines.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING HITS 1,283 G/T SILVER AND 0.83% TUNGSTEN IN SHALLOW HOLE — Northern Apollo Zone Extends 600m North; Colombia's First Hard-Rock Tungsten Find
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) has reported a new shallow, high-grade silver-tungsten zone in the Northern Apollo sector of its Guayabales project in Caldas, Colombia. The standout intercept from hole APC-186 returned 5.50m at 1,283 g/t silver, 0.83% WO₃, 0.57% copper and 0.17 g/t gold from just 89.15m depth — the highest silver grade ever reported from the project. The zone extends approximately 600 metres north of the existing Apollo Mineral Resource boundary, defining a new open system. Tungsten at commercial grades carries dual significance: it is the first hard-rock tungsten occurrence ever documented in Colombia, and tungsten is a NATO-designated critical mineral. A maiden NI 43-101 resource for Northern Apollo is targeted for mid-2027. Sixteen of 17 reported holes from the 2026 program returned intervals above the open-pit resource cutoff grade.

headline: LUNEX METALS RINGS THE TSXV BELL — New Argentine Gold-Silver Junior Lists Oct 30; Luna Roja Project Targets Epithermal System in Santa Cruz
snippet: Lunex Metals Corp (TSXV: LUNX) marked its TSX Venture Exchange debut with a market-open ceremony on October 30, 2026. The company is a Canadian gold and silver explorer targeting the Luna Roja project in Argentina's Santa Cruz province — the same prolific belt that hosts Newmont's Cerro Negro, AngloGold's Cerro Vanguardia, and Pan American Silver's Cerro Moro mine. Luna Roja is at an early exploration stage with geological mapping, sampling and ground geophysics completed; the listing proceeds fund an initial diamond drill program. Santa Cruz province has attracted major producer interest for high-grade low-sulfidation epithermal gold-silver systems at grassroots stage, making it a watch list for junior mining investors seeking pre-discovery entry points in a proven district.

headline: OIL SPIKE ADDS SECOND LAYER TO GOLD'S RATE HEADWIND — Rising Energy Costs Harden December Hike Bets; Miners Caught in Double Squeeze
snippet: Gold's decline to a one-year low on October 30 was driven not only by strong US growth and inflation data but also by escalating Middle East tensions pushing oil prices sharply higher — creating a dual inflation feedback loop that is hardening Federal Reserve December hike expectations. Higher energy costs feed directly into PCE inflation readings (September PCE already at 3.6% annually), which in turn raises the probability that the Fed will deliver a 25-basis-point hike in December after holding at 3.75–4.00% this week. That combination is pushing real interest rates higher and making yield-bearing assets more competitive against gold at the margin. The dynamic is particularly bearish for gold miners, which face both a softer gold price AND rising diesel, electricity, and consumables costs at mine sites — a margin squeeze that explains why gold equities are underperforming physical gold even on down days.

headline: SILVER BELOW $50: WHAT THE BREAK MEANS FOR JUNIOR MINERS — HSBC SEES MORE WEAKNESS; CONTRARIANS EYE RATIO ABOVE 77 AS HISTORIC REVERSAL SIGNAL
snippet: Silver's first close below US$50/oz since November 2025 is generating sharply divergent analyst views. HSBC sees further weakness with the Federal Reserve's hawkish shift and declining physical silver demand creating a dual headwind; the bank notes silver has declined approximately 9% year-to-date while gold remains up roughly 9% — an unusual divergence reflecting silver's higher exposure to slowing global manufacturing demand. The contrarian case: the gold-silver ratio has now climbed above 77:1, approaching levels that have historically marked major tops in the ratio and bottoms in both metals. The ratio's peaks in 2020 (above 120), 2016 (above 80) and 2008 (above 80) each preceded extended silver outperformance. For junior silver miners and developers — many of which carry valuations that have halved since Q1 — a ratio reversal would be a material re-rating catalyst. Physical retail demand at coin dealers is reportedly elevated on the dip.

headline: GALIANO GOLD Q3 RESULTS DUE NOVEMBER 5 — Watch for Recovery at Asanko After Q2 Crusher Downtime Cost 4% Throughput
snippet: Galiano Gold (TSX/NYSE-American: GAU) will release Q3 2026 results after market close on November 5, with a conference call scheduled for November 6 at 10:30 AM ET. The report is closely watched after Q2 saw a 4% sequential throughput decline at the Asanko mine in Ghana due to a failed ball mill gearbox and primary crusher pitman arm maintenance, which caused a slight EPS miss versus consensus despite full-year guidance being reaffirmed. Investors are looking for Q3 throughput recovery, cost normalisation, and any update on the biox circuit performance at Asanko. Galiano reports the same week as broader gold sector earnings clarity; Newmont already beat Q3 consensus on October 22 with adjusted EPS of US$2.20 versus US$1.94 expected, setting a constructive bar for the sector ahead of the rate-driven price correction that followed.

headline: PERSEUS MINING SECURES BACKUP POWER FOR NYANZAGA — Tanzania Gold Development Clears Key Infrastructure Hurdle; On Track for 2028 Production
snippet: Perseus Mining (ASX: PRU) confirmed on October 30 that it has secured backup power arrangements for its Nyanzaga gold development project in Tanzania, a key infrastructure milestone for a project that has faced power reliability questions in the country's grid. Reliable power is one of the top development risk factors for African mining projects, and securing backup capacity de-risks the construction timeline and operating cost profile. Nyanzaga contains approximately 6.5 million ounces of gold resources and is being advanced toward a construction decision, with first production targeted for 2028. Perseus already operates two producing gold mines in West Africa (Yaouré in Côte d'Ivoire and Edikan in Ghana) and its operational track record on the continent gives it credibility in advancing Tanzanian permitting and project execution.
